title: Supreme Court Remands Bannon Case for Further Consideration
description_short: The Supreme Court vacated the judgment under review in Bannon’s case and remanded it in light of a pending motion to dismiss the indictment.
description_medium: On April 6, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court granted Steve Bannon’s petition, vacated the D.C. Circuit judgment, and remanded the case for further consideration in light of a pending motion to dismiss the indictment. The docket records a remand; it does not say the indictment was dismissed or that the conviction was set aside.
description_long: On April 6, 2026, the Supreme Court granted Steve Bannon’s petition, vacated the judgment under review, and remanded the case for further consideration in light of a pending motion to dismiss the indictment. The Court’s docket identifies the lower court as the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit and records that its decision was dated May 10, 2024, with rehearing denied on May 27, 2025. The Supreme Court docket later records that judgment issued on May 8, 2026. These entries describe the case’s path through appellate review and its return for further consideration. They do not show that the district court granted the motion to dismiss, that the indictment was dismissed, or that Bannon’s conviction was overturned. The original entry also joined this criminal case to a separate civil presidential-records lawsuit and characterized the government’s actions as dismantling accountability. This narrower account records only the docketed Supreme Court action and leaves those other claims outside the supported copy.
organization_tags: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

title: White House Terminates Some U.S. Attorneys in February 2025
description_short: NBC reported the White House terminated as many as a dozen U.S. attorneys on February 12, 2025; the reported total was not established.
description_medium: On February 12, 2025, the White House terminated some U.S. attorneys during a wider change in federal prosecutorial leadership. NBC News reported terminations of as many as a dozen and said the precise total was not immediately available. Its account described immediate White House dismissals as a departure from the usual practice of Justice Department resignation requests.
description_long: On the evening of February 12, 2025, the White House terminated some U.S. attorneys during a transition in federal prosecutorial leadership. NBC News reported that the removals may have affected as many as a dozen offices and said its review found twelve names changed from a list published two days earlier. The Justice Department had not provided a total for how many of the nation’s 93 U.S. attorneys were affected. The article also noted that remaining Biden-nominated, Senate-confirmed attorneys were expected to leave, while immediate White House terminations departed from the usual practice of Justice Department resignation requests. This narrows the stored claim that all 93 attorneys were fired on January 20: the accessed reporting places terminations three weeks later and describes a limited number, not a complete one-day purge. It does not establish that all displaced attorneys were replaced by loyalists, that offices’ pending cases were left in limbo, or that prosecutors’ work was thereafter filtered through political loyalty. NBC reported that officials had not provided a final count. The account describes a personnel action and its reported departure from customary transitions, without asserting a legal finding about its propriety.
date_basis: The NBC article is dated February 13, 2025 and identifies the terminations as occurring Wednesday evening.
